body:
Bumps to `DocStringExtensions = "0.10"` and uses `$(MethodSignatures(; defaults = true))` ([JuliaDocs/DocStringExtensions.jl#194](https://github.com/JuliaDocs/DocStringExtensions.jl/pull/194)) for 143 docstrings whose signatures were hand-written only to show defaults. Many of those had gone stale (e.g. `FT = Float64` instead of `Oceananigans.defaults.FloatType`, missing keywords).

41 hand-written signatures stay, where the generated one would mislead: methods dispatching on a specific type (`set!(model::NonhydrostaticModel; ...)`), keywords hidden behind `kwargs...` (`NetCDFWriter`), and docstrings attached to a different method (`CFL`).

The `;` in `MethodSignatures(; defaults = true)` is needed: without it ExplicitImports reads `defaults = true` as an assignment and flags the import of `Oceananigans.defaults` as stale.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Generate docstring signatures with default values

body:
* `reset!` on a datetime clock should error. Right now it sets the clock to year 0. 
* datetime `Clock` `isapprox` throws currently because Julia has no `isapprox` for `DateTime`. For datetime clocks we should compare via `time_difference_seconds`
* When a `Simulation` is built with `minimum_relative_step` above `zero` and the step needed to land exactly on a stop time or output time is tiny, `run!` skips the step and advances the clock by hand with clock.time + Δt. That's DateTime + Float64, which has no method. The fix uses the same `next_time` helper the time steppers already use.
* A DateTime clock writes time as seconds since 2000-01-01 with that epoch in the units. The Zarr reader hands those seconds back as plain floats, so a FieldTimeSeries loaded from the store has float times. Any lookup like fts[Time(clock.time)] with a DateTime clock then fails, because it tries to subtract a float from a date. The fix decodes the units into dates on read, matching what NCDatasets does automatically for NetCDF.
* NetCDF read-back throws on uneven spacing. The NetCDF reader estimates the file's spacing as the mean difference of the times. With date times that mean is a Millisecond, and halving an odd number of milliseconds raises `InexactError`. Its missing-data warning also formats the time with a `%e printf`, which doesn't accept a date. The fix does the arithmetic in seconds.
title: close some gaps with `DateTime` clock
